title: Gov. Braun directs Indiana storm response and assesses damage in Northwest communities
text:
Gov. Braun directs Indiana storm response and assesses damage in Northwest communities
Governor Mike Braun directed state response efforts from Northwest Indiana on Aug. 12, assessing damage from recent severe storms and coordinating resources as widespread power outages, flooding, and storms continued across the state.
“Between storm damage, widespread power outages and flooding, hundreds of thousands of Hoosiers have been impacted across the state,” said Governor Braun. “I’ve directed our agencies to work around the clock alongside local officials, first responders and utility crews to get resources where they’re needed. As storms continue today, our teams are ready, resources are in place and we will continue responding to needs as they arise.”
Braun was joined by Adjutant General of the Indiana National Guard Larry Muennich, Indiana State Police Superintendent Anthony Scott, and Indiana Department of Homeland Security Executive Director Jonathan Whitham during meetings with local officials and first responders for updates on storm impacts and ongoing recovery efforts. The governor has tasked the Indiana Department of Homeland Security with leading statewide coordination alongside other agencies including Natural Resources, State Police, Transportation, and Correction departments. The State Emergency Operations Center raised its activation level to support response operations with generators and an oxygen trailer provided for Northwest Indiana.
Restoring power remains a top priority as utility crews work throughout affected areas. The American Red Cross is prepared to establish shelters, cooling centers, and charging stations if necessary while residents without electricity are encouraged to use available cooling centers due to heat concerns. Emergency teams are also responding beyond Northwest Indiana—particularly in Delaware and Henry counties—to address evolving conditions related to flooding.
As weather conditions persist across Indiana into Wednesday, Braun has instructed emergency teams to remain vigilant for additional risks such as further flooding or downed trees caused by saturated ground or strong winds. He urged residents to stay alert for emergency alerts, “Hoosiers should have multiple ways to receive emergency alerts, follow guidance from local authorities, never drive or walk through floodwaters, avoid downed power lines and dangerous road conditions,” he said.
Braun’s background includes public service roles on school boards and in state representation; he won election to the U.S. Senate in 2018 before becoming governor; he graduated summa cum laude from Wabash College with a degree in economics before earning an MBA from Harvard Business School; he expanded his company nationally employing thousands; championed over 40 bills that became law during his Senate term; has been married for 49 years raising four children—according to the official website.
